headline: A survey of healthcare executives found that half of organisations have cut staff because of AI or plan to within six months, starting with billing and claims teams.
score_reason: Wide-reaching jobs finding, but an executive survey relayed by a niche outlet; kept at the curator score.
importance_line: Points to AI reshaping hospital and insurer back-office jobs before clinical care, but this is a survey of executives, not counted layoffs, and the report itself warns of a shortage of trained coders.
source: Outsource Accelerator, citing Bessemer Venture Partners and Bain & Company
summary: Outsource Accelerator reports, citing the 2026 Healthcare AI ROI Scorecard from Bessemer Venture Partners and Bain & Company, a survey of 226 executives at health systems, insurers and drug companies, that half of the organisations have cut staff because of AI or plan to within six months, with cuts averaging 8% to 13% of the affected functions. Among providers cutting jobs, 73% named billing and revenue-cycle work, although the report warns that "healthcare has no surplus of administrative workers to shed", noting a roughly 30% shortage of medical coders.
notes: Bessemer/Bain report not opened; figures as relayed by Outsource Accelerator.
